import os
import re

html_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\YouTube.html"
output_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\.gemini\antigravity\brain\7a78deb3-fd50-47e2-8d2a-a23cba5ad928\youtube_videos.md"

os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(output_path), exist_ok=True)

with open(html_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore') as f:
    content = f.read()

# YouTube titles often look like "Title by Channel views time"
# Let's try to extract aria-labels containing " by " and " views "
matches = re.findall(r'aria-label="([^"]+ by [^"]+ views [^"]+)"', content)

# Sometimes "views" is missing for livestreams or premieres
# Let's also just grab anything with " by " that looks long enough
if not matches:
    matches = set(re.findall(r'aria-label="([^"]+ by [^"]+)"', content))

# Keep unique matches only
unique_matches = []
seen = set()
for m in matches:
    # unescape html entities
    m = m.replace('&', '&').replace('"', '"').replace(''', "'")
    if m not in seen:
        seen.add(m)
        unique_matches.append(m)

# Format the results
markdown = "# YouTube Videos List\n\nHere are the videos extracted from your saved YouTube page:\n\n"
for m in unique_matches:
    # Attempt to split title and channel
    # "Title by Channel 10,000 views..."
    parts = m.split(' by ')
    if len(parts) >= 2:
        title = parts[0]
        rest = ' by '.join(parts[1:])
        markdown += f"- **{title}** by {rest}\n"
    else:
        markdown += f"- {m}\n"

with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write(markdown)

print(f"Extracted {len(unique_matches)} videos to markdown file.")

import os
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import re

html_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\YouTube.html"
output_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\.gemini\antigravity\brain\7a78deb3-fd50-47e2-8d2a-a23cba5ad928\youtube_videos.md"

with open(html_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore') as f:
    soup = BeautifulSoup(f, 'html.parser')

videos = []
for a in soup.find_all('a', id='video-title-link'):
    title = a.get('title', '').strip()
    if not title:
        title = a.text.strip()
    
    # Try to find channel
    channel = "Unknown Channel"
    parent = a.find_parent('ytd-rich-item-renderer')
    if not parent:
        parent = a.find_parent('ytd-rich-grid-media')
    
    if parent:
        channel_elem = parent.find('ytd-channel-name')
        if channel_elem:
            channel = channel_elem.text.strip()
            # remove extra whitespace
            channel = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', channel)
    
    videos.append(f"- **{title}** | {channel}")

if not videos:
    # try another way: all a tags with title, except UI elements
    ui_titles = {'YouTube', 'Search', 'Home', 'Shorts', 'Subscriptions', 'You', 'Your channel', 'History', 'Playlists', 'Watch later', 'Liked videos', 'Trending', 'Music', 'Gaming', 'News', 'Sports'}
    for a in soup.find_all('a', title=True):
        title = a['title'].strip()
        if title and title not in ui_titles:
            # Check if it looks like a video link
            if '/watch?v=' in a.get('href', ''):
                videos.append(f"- **{title}**")

# Still no videos? Try finding ytd-rich-grid-media or ytd-video-renderer
if not videos:
    for node in soup.find_all(['ytd-rich-item-renderer', 'ytd-video-renderer']):
        title_node = node.select_one('#video-title, #video-title-link')
        title = title_node.text.strip() if title_node else None
        
        channel_node = node.select_one('ytd-channel-name yt-formatted-string, ytd-channel-name a')
        channel = channel_node.text.strip() if channel_node else None
        
        if title:
            videos.append(f"- **{title}** | {channel or 'Unknown Channel'}")

# Clean up newlines in titles
videos = [v.replace('\n', ' ') for v in set(videos)]

with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write("# YouTube Videos List\n\n")
    for v in videos:
        f.write(v + "\n")

print(f"Extracted {len(videos)} videos to {output_path}")

import json
import re

html_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\YouTube.html"
output_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\.gemini\antigravity\brain\7a78deb3-fd50-47e2-8d2a-a23cba5ad928\youtube_videos.md"

with open(html_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore') as f:
    content = f.read()

# Find ytInitialData
match = re.search(r'var ytInitialData = (\{.*?\});</script>', content, re.DOTALL)
if not match:
    # Try another common pattern
    match = re.search(r'window\["ytInitialData"\] = (\{.*?\});', content, re.DOTALL)

if not match:
    print("Could not find ytInitialData")
    exit(1)

try:
    data = json.loads(match.group(1))
except json.JSONDecodeError:
    print("Failed to parse ytInitialData")
    exit(1)

# We need to recursively search the JSON for video titles and channel names
videos = []
def extract_videos(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        # Check if this dict represents a video
        if 'videoId' in obj and 'title' in obj and 'runs' in obj['title']:
            title = "".join(r.get('text', '') for r in obj['title']['runs'])
            
            # Find channel name, usually under 'ownerText' or 'longBylineText' or 'shortBylineText'
            channel = "Unknown Channel"
            for key in ['ownerText', 'longBylineText', 'shortBylineText']:
                if key in obj and 'runs' in obj[key]:
                    channel = "".join(r.get('text', '') for r in obj[key]['runs'])
                    break
            
            if title:
                videos.append((title, channel))
                
        for k, v in obj.items():
            extract_videos(v)
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        for item in obj:
            extract_videos(item)

extract_videos(data)

# Remove duplicates
unique_videos = list(dict.fromkeys(videos))

with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write("# YouTube Videos List\n\nHere are the videos extracted from your saved YouTube page:\n\n")
    for title, channel in unique_videos:
        f.write(f"- **{title}** | Channel: {channel}\n")

print(f"Extracted {len(unique_videos)} videos to {output_path}")

from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import re

html_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\Downloads\YouTube.html"
output_path = r"C:\Users\renu5\.gemini\antigravity\brain\7a78deb3-fd50-47e2-8d2a-a23cba5ad928\youtube_videos.md"

with open(html_path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='ignore') as f:
    soup = BeautifulSoup(f, 'html.parser')

videos = []

# Method 1: All a tags with href containing watch or shorts
for a in soup.find_all('a', href=True):
    href = a['href']
    if '/watch' in href or '/shorts/' in href:
        title = a.get('title')
        aria_label = a.get('aria-label')
        
        # if there's aria-label, it usually has "Title by Channel views ago"
        text = aria_label or title or a.text.strip()
        if text:
            # clean up newlines
            text = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', text)
            if len(text) > 5:  # skip UI things
                videos.append(text)

# Method 2: ytLockupMetadataViewModelHeadingReset
for h3 in soup.find_all('h3', class_=lambda c: c and 'ytLockupMetadataViewModelHeadingReset' in c):
    title = h3.get('title')
    if title:
        videos.append(title.strip())

# Method 3: id="video-title"
for elem in soup.find_all(id='video-title'):
    title = elem.text.strip()
    if title:
        videos.append(re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', title))

# Deduplicate
unique_vids = []
seen = set()
for v in videos:
    v = v.replace('&', '&').replace('"', '"').replace(''', "'")
    if v not in seen and v not in ["Shorts", "Play all", "Watch later", "Save to playlist", "Share", "More actions", "Report"]:
        seen.add(v)
        unique_vids.append(v)

with open(output_path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    f.write("# YouTube Videos List\n\nHere are the videos extracted from your saved YouTube page:\n\n")
    for v in unique_vids:
        # If it looks like "Title by Channel X views", format it nicely
        if ' by ' in v and (' views' in v or ' ago' in v):
            parts = v.split(' by ')
            title = parts[0]
            rest = ' by '.join(parts[1:])
            f.write(f"- **{title}** | {rest}\n")
        else:
            f.write(f"- {v}\n")

print(f"Extracted {len(unique_vids)} videos to {output_path}")
args.Description: DOM extraction script for YouTube videos.
